explanation.en: A singleton is created once by the root provider and every later resolve returns that same object, so both variables point at one Clock.
A transient service is constructed on every resolve. Three GetRequiredService calls run the constructor three times.
A scoped service is one instance per scope: a and b come from the same scope, c from a new one. In ASP.NET Core each HTTP request is a scope.
Both registrations are kept. Resolving a single IGreeter returns the LAST one registered (Fr), while GetServices returns all of them, in registration order.
TryAdd* registers only when the service type has no registration yet. IStore already has one, so MemStore is skipped: one descriptor, SqlStore.
Middleware runs in registration order on the way in and unwinds in reverse on the way out: code after await next() runs once the inner part of the pipeline has finished.
No middleware ends the pipeline, so next() reaches the terminal delegate that Build() appends. With no endpoint selected, it sets the status code to 404.

Configuration providers are layered: a source added later overrides the same key from an earlier one. Keys it does not define (Host) still come from the earlier source. That is how environment variables override appsettings.json.
GetValue converts the string "3" to an int. A missing key gives default(int), which is 0, unless you pass your own default value, here 30.

The colon is the hierarchy separator, so Db:Host and Db:Port are two children of a Db section. Keys are case-insensitive. A section that only has children has no value of its own, so config["Db"] is null.
Binding sets only the properties the section contains. Port is overwritten with 2525; UseSsl has no key, so it keeps its initializer value, true.
All Configure actions run first, in registration order, and only then every PostConfigure, regardless of where it was registered.

The minimum level, Warning, applies to every category without a more specific rule. The "Db" filter matches categories starting with Db, so Db.Query logs from Debug up, but Trace is still below Debug.
Cancel() runs the registered callbacks synchronously, printing A. Registering on a token that is already cancelled runs the callback immediately, so B prints before the final 1.
Hosted services start one after another in registration order and stop in reverse order, so the service started last is stopped first.
